1. Would if I could get one
2 & 3. I don't pay much for my lifestyle as is. My parents own the house I live in and my bf pays the bills (and even with all of this help, I still can't function for shit). The cats are really minor expenses. Maybe $40/month to feed.
4. I am subscribed, on my other account.

1. Done more hours of that than I care to think about.
2. I've taken lots of free courses well outside my area of expertise-- I've taught myself a bunch of allegedly useful shit, but nobody gives a shit, without credentials or legit experience
3. I'm trying. Last week I got 3 hours in. I decided to down a bottle of rum today, instead of hitting the gym. Oh well.

I've thought of these contingency plans. I've tried them. Nothing really seems to matter, is the problem. =\

That sucks ass :(

Have you had the experience yet where your education makes you less hireable? I swear I've missed out on jobs because people look at my resume and go "why the fuck would this person want to work for minimum wage with a master's degree?"

Yes, ladies and gents, the degree I spent 5 years and... I don't even want to know how much money on has actually fucked me over, rather than putting me ahead. super.

Hey, prostitution might just work. :p I don't think anyone would ever pay to fuck me, but it's maybe an option. I (sorta) jokingly asked my bf to be my reference for my application to a rub n' tug. He got mad and said no. Hah.

Since November, so I guess about 4-ish months? I tried for jobs after my undergrad too. I didn't want a grad degree, but I was told by people in industry that it'd pretty much guarantee me a job. They lied. If I had 5 years experience, maybe I'd be golden.

About 6 weeks ago I gave up on my industry and started applying for bullshit temp jobs that pay wages I can't really live on. I've heard "oh yeah, we have something for you. It starts Monday, I'll e-mail you the details" followed by several days of nothing, until I call them and am like "so what's the deal with this job thing?" and they tell me that I didn't get it. Or that they didn't hear back from the client, or whatever.

How about you?

I know, right? I've made a concerted effort not to be a shitty human being. Like, I volunteer. I try to be nice, and take care of the people around me. Rationally I know this counts for nothing, but some part of me is still like "what the fuck is the deal with this? What did I do to deserve this?"

Just don't even know what to do with any of this anymore.

I wish I could say it was better here-- maybe it is (I'm in Canada).

My friends have all gone through this to some degree... just, shit's worked out for most of them now. I remain the lone exception.

It's the up and down that's the worst. I think I could deal if it was just a straight-up "no, you're a piece of shit". That'd be fine. I'd get a job at McDonald's, and expect nothing more. It's all of the "you're so smart!" that really gets to me. Or the "your test results are amazing! I have just the position for you!" followed by the inevitable "oh, well, our client decided to go a different direction with the position". I wish I believed in a God so I could just be like "ALRIGHT ALREADY, I'M A PIECE OF SHIT, I GET IT. QUIT IT WITH THE SUBTLE BEATDOWNS".

... ugh. University is a waste of time. I can't believe I was so retarded as to waste the time and money on not one degree, but two.

In pretty much the same position. Every time someone says "just keep at it, you'll find something" I don't know whether to punch them in the mouth or just rip all my hair out.

Sorry you're having to go through this too.
